top_choice_rationale: P001 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clock) rewards a specific and non-obvious idea: a magic wavelength at which the trap shifts both clock levels equally, so thousands of atoms can be interrogated free of first-order light shift and motional broadening, with residual shifts controlled at the 1e-18 level. It is mature and independently reproduced and compared by several laboratories, and the two-name allocation (Katori for concept and first demonstration, Ye for accuracy and stability) has no arbitrary cut, with a citation that can name the lattice and so separate it from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-system prizes. P002 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) is a high-quality Z2 and HgTe achievement but its credit (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Hasan, Fu, Moore) and its overlap with the 2016 prize remain unresolved, so it ranks second, ahead of no award.
recusal_note: No connection to Katori or Ye or the lattice-clock community apparent from profile; long-time collaborator of Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) and of the Lund and ETH attosecond groups, which is not relevant to P001 or P002; no tie to Kane, Mele or Molenkamp.
